title.title: The Bass trace conjecture for every discrete group
title.subtitle: Claim: traces of idempotents over $\ell^1(G)$ see only finite-order elements; for torsion-free $G$, only 0 and 1

plain: In a torsion-free group's algebra, the only 'projections' are the trivial ones, 0 and 1

lines.tex: \mathrm{HS}(e) \text{ lives on conjugacy classes of finite-order elements}

beats.text: Take an idempotent matrix over the group algebra
Bass: its Hattori–Stallings trace sees only elements of finite order
For a torsion-free group that leaves only 0 and 1: Kaplansky's idempotent conjecture

voice.text: The Bass trace conjecture, every group.
Bass: the trace of an idempotent sees only elements of finite order.
For torsion-free groups, idempotents are then zero and one.
Claimed: the analytic version holds for every discrete group.

sources.quote: Bass conjectured in 1976 that the Hattori–Stallings trace of a projective module over a group ring sees only elements of finite order.
Over $\mathbb C$ both were known for groups satisfying Baum–Connes-type hypotheses (Berrick, Chatterji and Mislin for $\ell^1$-Bass).
The family headline is the $\ell^1$-Bass conjecture for every discrete group, which is analytic and not formalized.
for torsion-free $G$ that the only idempotents of $RG$ are 0 and 1, for every commutative domain $R$ of characteristic 0
